title: What is the area of a triangle with base 8 and height 5?
description: A triangle has a base of eight centimetres and a height of five centimetres. A rectangle drawn around it has area forty square centimetres, and the triangle is half of that. Keeko doubts this and says the triangle is forty square centimetres.
teaching_notes: One idea: the triangle is half of the rectangle drawn on the same base with the same height, so its area is half of base times height. Watch for children who give the area of the whole rectangle.

source: A triangle has base 8 cm and height 5 cm. Find its area.
video_script.why: The child knows a triangle on the bottom side of a rectangle covers half of it, and uses this with a measured base and height.
video_script.substitution: Draw the rectangle round the triangle, find its area, then take half.
video_script.anchor: the triangle of the book with base eight centimetres and height five centimetres
video_script.wrong_answer: the triangle is forty square centimetres
video_script.wrong_move: Keeko gives the triangle the area of the whole rectangle around it. The corners outside the triangle are not part of it, so only half of the rectangle belongs to the triangle.
video_script.payoff_line: the area of the triangle is twenty square centimetres
hold_back: the area of the triangle is 20 cm²
never_show: the area of the triangle, before the answer beat
maths_rules: triangle with base 8 cm and height 5 cm; the rectangle drawn around it has the same base and height
the triangle is half of the outer rectangle
the two corner pieces outside the triangle together make the other 20 cm²
video_script.design: One idea: the triangle is half of the rectangle round it. Wrong idea: the triangle takes the whole rectangle. The triangle stays on stage from the hook to the end.

narration: <bookmark mark='doubt'/>Keeko thinks the triangle is forty square centimetres, because eight times five is forty.
<bookmark mark='corners'/>Forty is the whole rectangle. The two corners outside the triangle are not part of it.
<bookmark mark='fix'/>The triangle has only half of the rectangle, and half of forty is twenty.
